This article builds a small cohort from the open MIMIC-IV demo, end to end: a
project folder, the raw files, the cohort, the harmonized tables, and a first
look at the data. It takes a few minutes and needs no PhysioNet account. Every
output below was produced by running the code shown.

## What you need

- R 4.1 or later, with rendehR installed:

  ```r
  install.packages("pak")
  pak::pak("ATE-DRIVEN-lab/rendehR", dependencies = TRUE)
  ```

  `dependencies = TRUE` also installs the suggested packages, among them
  ggplot2 for the plot below and shiny for the explorer.

- A running PostgreSQL server on which your login may create databases.
  rendehR does not install or start PostgreSQL; it connects to a server you
  run, and creates the database it is told to use. The README's
  [Requirements](https://ate-driven-lab.github.io/rendehR/#requirements)
  section shows how to install one on macOS, Windows, Linux or Docker.
  Check that it answers before you start:

  ```r
  con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "postgres",
                        host = "localhost", port = 5432,
                        user = "postgres", password = "your-password")
  DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
  ```

  An error such as "connection refused" means no server is running at that
  address.

## Create a project

A project is a folder that holds the configuration, the raw files and the
cohort files. `ehr_init_project()` creates it:


``` r
library(rendehR)
ehr_init_project(src_name = "mimic_iv_demo", base_dir = "rendehr-demo")
```



Two files in `rendehr-demo/config/` need your attention. In `ehr_config.json`,
set the database rendehR should use (it is created on first use). This tutorial
also sets `cohort.profile` to `"scid"`, the SCI reference implementation, so the
clinical enrichment stages run; new projects default to `"generic"`.

```json
"database": {
  "db_name": "rendehr_demo",
  "credentials_path": "config/config_pass.json"
}
```

and put your PostgreSQL login in `config_pass.json` (the `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`,
`PGUSER` and `PGPASSWORD` environment variables override it):

```json
{
  "postgres": {"host": "localhost", "port": 5432, "user": "postgres", "password": "..."}
}
```

Then make it the active project, so later calls know where the files and the
database are:


``` r
ehr_use_config("rendehr-demo/config/ehr_config.json")
```

## Download the demo

The MIMIC-IV demo has 100 patients and is open to everyone. `download_source()`
fetches it into the project and checks every file against the release
checksums:


``` r
download_source("mimic_iv_demo")
```


``` r
list.files("rendehr-demo/data/source_data/mimic_iv_demo/icu")
#> [1] "caregiver.csv.gz"        "chartevents.csv.gz"      "d_items.csv.gz"         
#> [4] "datetimeevents.csv.gz"   "icustays.csv.gz"         "ingredientevents.csv.gz"
#> [7] "inputevents.csv.gz"      "outputevents.csv.gz"     "procedureevents.csv.gz"
```

## Build a cohort

rendehR defines the cohort first and only then imports the rows that belong to
it. Two cohorts come with the package:


``` r
list_example_cohorts()[, c("name", "kind", "description")]
#>      name kind
#> 1    scid  icd
#> 2 sepsis3  sql
#>                                                                 description
#> 1 Spinal cord injury - bundled ICD-9/10 list (the package reference cohort)
#> 2  Sepsis-3 (Singer 2016): SOFA >= 2 + suspicion of infection, per ICU stay
```

`run_one_source()` takes one source through every stage: it imports the
Sepsis-3 cohort to Parquet, loads it into PostgreSQL, builds the visit windows
and the cohort table, extracts the clinical concepts and writes the harmonized
tables.


``` r
stages <- run_one_source(
  "mimic_iv_demo",
  cohort_selection = cohort_selection_options(cohort = "sepsis3")
)
```


``` r
stages[, c("stage", "status", "seconds")]
#>                       stage  status     seconds
#> 1     import_cohort_general success 13.84079146
#> 2                    run_db success  7.47663093
#> 3              run_raw_mods success  0.01454449
#> 4       build_window_tables success  0.02767563
#> 5 build_cohort_info_general success  1.35248709
#> 6         run_comorbidities success  0.25613403
#> 7                   run_iss success  1.24396586
#> 8              run_concepts success 18.57952905
#> 9     run_harmonized_tables success  0.76335311
```

To combine sources, and to get the analysis tables, merge them into one schema.
With a single source this still gives the tables everything else reads:


``` r
merge_sources("mimic_iv_demo")
```

## Read the data

`ehr_connect()` keeps the connection details for the functions that read data;
with an active project it needs no arguments.


``` r
ehr_connect()
cohort <- load_merged_cohort_info("rendehr")
nrow(cohort)
#> [1] 36
length(unique(cohort$src_patient_id))
#> [1] 31
```

The demo has 39 ICU stays that meet Sepsis-3 in 31 patients; the cohort table
holds their hospital admissions. One row per admission, with demographics and
outcomes:


``` r
flat <- load_merged_flat("rendehr")
flat[1:5, c("src_patient_id", "age", "sex", "admission_type", "hospital_los", "hospital_mortality")]
#>   src_patient_id  age    sex admission_type hospital_los hospital_mortality
#> 1       10002428 81.4 female      emergency        10.98              FALSE
#> 2       10002428 81.3 female      emergency        17.09              FALSE
#> 3       10002495 81.4   male         urgent         6.89              FALSE
#> 4       10003400 75.1 female         urgent        23.24              FALSE
#> 5       10003400 75.6 female         urgent        29.71               TRUE
```

Measurements come as a long table of `concept_name`, time and value, or reshaped
wide into time bins. Here, the extremes of the first 24 hours after admission:


``` r
day1 <- load_merged_ts_wide(
  "rendehr",
  spec    = list(heart_rate = c("min", "max"), lactate = "max", spo2 = "min"),
  bin_min = 24 * 60,
  window  = c(0, 0)
)
head(day1)
#>              ehr_id   source_data src_patient_id src_admission_id t_bin heart_rate_min
#> 1 10002428_23473524 mimic_iv_demo       10002428         23473524     0             67
#> 2 10002428_28662225 mimic_iv_demo       10002428         28662225     0            100
#> 3 10002495_24982426 mimic_iv_demo       10002495         24982426     0             83
#> 4 10004235_24181354 mimic_iv_demo       10004235         24181354     0            101
#> 5 10004720_22081550 mimic_iv_demo       10004720         22081550     0             68
#> 6 10004733_27411876 mimic_iv_demo       10004733         27411876     0             82
#>   heart_rate_max lactate spo2
#> 1            109     1.5   96
#> 2            135     2.4   90
#> 3            133     4.4   84
#> 4            144     4.5   90
#> 5             86     2.2   93
#> 6            107     0.8   90
```


``` r
library(ggplot2)
d <- merge(day1, flat[, c("ehr_id", "hospital_mortality")], by = "ehr_id")
d <- d[is.finite(d$lactate), ]
ggplot(d, aes(factor(hospital_mortality, labels = c("Survived", "Died")), lactate)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Highest lactate, first 24 h (mmol/L)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Explore it

The cohort explorer opens the same tables in the browser: cohort overview,
filters and a characteristics table, outcomes and survival, one patient's
timeline, the concept inventory.

```r
run_explorer("rendehr")
```

See `vignette("explorer", package = "rendehR")` for a tour.
